title: Ang 1370–1377: Kabir's saloks, second half
hookLine: including where there is forgiveness, there the Lord is
tomorrow: a Sufi saint says: look under your own collar. what's under there?

cards: Someone in the family group chat finally types sorry, and the chat goes quiet, everyone waiting to see who answers first. Kabir has a couplet for that silence, on ang 1372.
In paraphrase: where there's wisdom, there's dharma; where there's lying, there's wrong; where there's greed, there's death. And where there's forgiveness, there is the Lord himself.
That answers yesterday's question: the Lord isn't in a place. The Lord is in a moment.

teach.b: It's a list of four, and the last one surprises. Wisdom, lies and greed are things people do or fall into.

So is forgiveness, and that's where Kabir finds the Lord: not up a mountain, not inside a building, but in the moment someone lets a debt go. The couplet doesn't say forget. It doesn't say pretend it never happened.
It says where forgiveness is, the Lord is there too.
And it gathers the week. The one light at dawn: every person from the same light. Beni's mirror: what's under the marks.
The last raga and its two ways of singing. The old style, in the room's accent. The tiny poems that stop at the right place.
Kabir at the bottom of the list.
Forgiveness sits easily beside every one of them. If everyone comes from one light, and everyone else is good, then forgiving is a way of seeing straight.

how: Sikhs quote Kabir's couplet 'where there is forgiveness, there the Lord is' in talks and kirtan; khimaa, forgiveness, is named among the virtues across the Granth.

o: where Kabir finds the Lord where forgiveness is
where Kabir says I'm the worst of all
where Farid says look under your own collar

games.q: Kabir's list on ang 1372 — tap the pairs.

s: Kabir's couplet says to forgive and forget
it says where forgiveness is, the Lord is. it never says forget or pretend.
in Kabir's couplet, where there's greed there's death
wisdom, lies, greed, forgiveness: and the last one is where the Lord is.

games.q: a friend took credit for your idea, then apologized. she's waiting for an answer. what does Kabir's couplet point you to?
o: forgive, without pretending it didn't happen; that's where Kabir finds the Lord.
forgive only once she makes it up in public; then it really counts.
say it's fine and never bring it up again, even if it isn't fine.
games.why: Kabir puts the Lord in the moment of forgiveness. nothing in the couplet asks you to pretend, or to wait for a public payback first.

practice: Close your eyes and let one small grudge come to mind, the kind you could set down someday. Don't decide anything. Just hold it next to Kabir's line, where there is forgiveness, and breathe slowly until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1370. The second half of Kabir's couplets, where the Lord is found where forgiveness is.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: khimaa, forgiveness, from Kabir's couplet on ang 1372: where there is forgiveness, there the Lord is.

carryVoice: Keep this close: where there is forgiveness, because that's where Kabir puts the Lord. See you next week.
